Exceptions to the rules
Credit hasn't blinkedHY spreads near record tights while the Fed hikes into 41.6× CAPE. Credit is either right (no recession) or the last to know — no middle ground at these spreads. Confirm: Spreads stay contained through the next hike. · Refute: Credit proxy breaks >2.5% below its 50-day average.
Narrow leadership, complacent volMag7 correcting while the index holds and VIX sleeps — distribution-phase behavior wearing an expansion-phase mask. Confirm: Mag7 gap narrows below 5 pts (breadth healing). · Refute: Gap widens past 12 pts (rollover risk).
The long end is doing the tightening10Y at 5.16% vs funds at 3.75–4.00% prices fiscal risk, not just Fed policy — a term-premium revolt, not a normal hiking cycle. Confirm: 10Y rolls over on soft CPI. · Refute: 10Y prints new highs into further hikes.
Historical analogs
1999–2000 — closest rhymeCAPE ~44 then vs 41.6 now; narrow must-own leadership; Fed hiking into strength; credit calm until it wasn't. Confirm: Credit widens while the index holds. · Refute: Breadth heals and the Fed pauses.
2018 Q4 — the mechanism to fearHiking on autopilot into rich valuations; −20% in a quarter; credit serene weeks earlier. Confirm: Hawkish surprise plus vol spike. · Refute: Fed signals pause.
1994–95 — comforting, likely wrongAggressive hikes and bond pain, but CAPE was 24× and the hikes actually slowed the economy — transmission worked. This cycle's broken transmission cuts both ways. Confirm: Economy absorbs hikes; 1995-style rip follows. · Refute: Transmission was just lagged — the break arrives late.

Full A1–F phase guide
A1 · CapitulationPanic selling; prices bottom as the weak hands give up.
A2 · AccumulationPatient money buys quietly while the crowd stays scared.
B · RecoveryPrices start climbing; the worst looks over.
C · VerificationThe rally gets tested. Is the recovery real?
D · Expansion — we are hereBroad participation; new money flows in, leadership widens.
E · EuphoriaEveryone is bullish; the peak forms.
F · DistributionSmart money sells into strength; the decline begins.

What happened
Sep 16 FOMC FOMC Decision + SEP decided

Outcome Raised the federal funds target range 25bp to 3.75–4.00%, unanimous 12-0 vote — the Fed's first rate hike in three years. New SEP median points to 4.1% at end of 2026 and 2027, with the longer-run rate at 3.2%.

Market reaction Widely anticipated (markets had ~83–85% odds of the hike priced going in); the unanimity was the surprise. Markets repriced toward one more 25bp hike in December.

Now · Sep 2026 — where you are

Fed funds 3.75–4.00% (Sep 16 hike; down from the 5.14% 2024 peak) · HY spreads ~278bps, near the tightest in the post-1997 record · CAPE 41.6×, second-highest since 1881 · SPX ~7,704. The period to compare against is 1994–95 — the last time the Fed tightened aggressively while equities kept climbing (rates 4.2%→5.8%, SPX +34%, spreads calm). Key difference: CAPE was ~24× then vs 41.6× now. A slower-tightening alternative: 2015–19 (rates 0.1%→2.2%, SPX +58%, CAPE 24×→30×).

Pattern emerging

Rate cuts without a credit scare. The Fed cut from 5.14% to ~3.5% through mid-2026, then hiked to 3.75–4.00% on Sep 16, while HY spreads stayed near record tights and equities pushed to record valuation. The 2001 and 2008 cutting cycles arrived with spreads peaking near 912bps and 1,725bps — this cycle never widened. What to watch: HY OAS widening past ~400–600bps, M2 growth stalling from +4.6%, or SPX losing its 200-day. This is an analog, not a prediction — at 41.6× CAPE the margin for error is thin.

Phase D Projection · Three Models · 2026–2030

S&P 500 Projection

Three independent models — EPS × P/E, CAPE reversion, and institutional — each drawn as a band from its bear to its bull scenario. The band is the honest part: one line to the moon would be a lie.

How to read this chart: each shaded band is one model. Its bottom edge = bear scenario, its top edge = bull scenario, its center line = the scenario selected below. Where bands overlap, the models agree; where they don't, that's genuine uncertainty.
Model 1 · EPS × P/E

In: FactSet EPS trajectory × Goldman P/E path. Out: year-end S&P 500 price.

Model 2 · CAPE reversion

In: current CAPE 41.6× pulled toward its long-run average at a chosen speed + EPS growth. Out: implied price level.

Model 3 · Institutional

In: Vanguard / Research Affiliates / GMO annualized return forecasts. Out: price range from compounding today's level.
